notes:
Overview:
- Mid-market product analytics SaaS serving B2B product teams (feature usage + in-app help). Evaluating Redwood for fast vector search + chat-based help in product console.
- Primary interest: start on Hosted API to validate UX, then move to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost once usage reaches steady state.

Key stakeholders:
- CTO: Priya Balan (owns infra + ops decisions) — "We need predictable p99 latency under 200ms for in-app suggestions."
- Head of Product: Marco Reyes (owns UX/metrics) — wants sub-100ms median for inline search.
- Engineering lead: Sean O'Rourke (platform) — focused on KV cache and autoscaling.

POC & Demo history (timeline):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (AE Maya) — qualifying: current ML infra on GCP, ~350 engineers + product org of 40.
- 2025-12-05: Hosted API demo (Maya + Liam) — quick integration (2 endpoints) with Product staging; demo captured in ff_2026-02-18.
- 2026-01-10: Security questionnaire submitted; initial SOC2 docs provided.
- 2026-01-22: Price sensitivity call — finance flagged token costs if usage grows 10x. Requested dedicated pricing band.
- 2026-02-14: POC kickoff — ingest 1.2M support docs into embeddings index; latency targets defined (median <100ms for search, p99 <250ms).
- 2026-02-28: First POC results: batching reduced token cost by ~18% for search workload; KV prefix caching cut repeated-context cost by ~12% on average. Details in attached Drive doc.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing follow-up with Solutions Finance — discussed committed capacity vs burst pricing for Dedicated.

Cost-optimization workshop (requested during evaluation):
- Objective: quantify unit economics and operational levers to stay within finance ARR target while meeting latency SLOs.
- Attendees requested: Priya (CTO), Sean (Eng lead), Marco (Head of Product), Finance (2), Maya (AE), Liam (SE), Redwood Optimize rep.
- Agenda proposed:
  1) Workload profile review (tokens/seq len/arrival patterns)
  2) Batching policy simulation (latency vs throughput trade-offs)
  3) Cache and prefix reuse strategies (prefix/KV caching effects and TTLs)
  4) Quantization profiles for model variants (FP16 vs 4-bit/8-bit ops)
  5) Dedicated capacity sizing & committed discount modeling
  6) Implementation roadmap + telemetry needed for eval
- Expected deliverables: a slide with recommended batching and cache config, quantization profile suggestions per model, expected $/M tokens and 12-month cost projection (hosted vs dedicated), and clear checklist for security sign-off.

Technical requirements & preferences:
- Models: prefer open Llama-family variants for customization; may accept Redwood-verified smaller models for cheap embeddings but want fallback to larger generator for complex responses.
- Routing: region-aware routing for EU customers; fallback to lower-cost variant when Dedicated pool is saturated.
- Data handling: retention max 90 days in staging, EU residency for EU customer data. KMS integration required.

Quotes & snippets from calls:
- Priya (CTO): "We can tolerate slight quality drop for cheaper models on non-critical flows but can't on in-product help answers."
- Marco (Head product): "If median latency is under 100ms the team will greenlight inline suggestions in Q3."
